obligation: G3 -- shared-program MLP, verified at FULL 64-layer scale
what: One shared SwiGLU operator (gate/up/down) reused across ALL 64 layers + per-layer FiLM code (gamma,beta), trained on 64-layer pooled MLP teacher function, held-out on unseen tokens.
setup: 64 layers x 2000 tokens; 80/20 token split -> train 102400, held 25600. Teacher F(h)=down(silu(gate@h)*up@h). q3 control = group-64 absmax 3-level on each of gate/up/down.
headline: At full 64-layer scale a single shared operator (m=6144, 38.3 MB group-64 q3 + 1.6 MB codes) BEATS the q3 control held-out (0.371 vs 0.384) at 35% of q3 active MLP bytes = 2.8x fewer MLP DRAM bytes/token. The q3 active-byte wall is broken at FULL scale, not just the 15 self-similar layers of the first G3 preview.
honest_downgrade: The 15-layer preview reported 24% active bytes and a 0.026 generalization gap. Those 15 layers (L4,8..60) are more self-similar than all 64. At full scale the operator needs m=6144 not 4096 (35% not 24%) and shows a large train/held gap (0.074 vs 0.371) = pure token-memorization, i.e. regularization headroom. The core claim (shared operator beats q3 held-out at far fewer active bytes) holds and is now proven at full scale.
physics_projection: MLP is ~7 GB of the q3 token's ~11.7 GB active bytes. Shared-op MLP = 38.3 MB if cache-resident across 64 dispatches, or ~2.45 GB if re-read per layer. Cache-resident -> token active ~4.74 GB -> ~2.5x TPS -> ~75-85 TPS. Not cache-resident -> ~7.15 GB -> ~1.6x -> ~50 TPS. Either is a real successor; the Metal residency measurement (G10) decides which.

regularization/mixture: the 0.30 train/held gap says weight-decay + early-stop (tuned run in flight, saving checkpoints) and possibly a K=2 operator split (mixture, G6) can push held-out below 0.371.
G2 task-family split: captures are prose-heavy; cross-task (code/reasoning) generalization untested.
